pr_title: Restore low battery state on ISY994 Insteon heartbeat nodes
pr_body:

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Restore the state of an Insteon Heartbeat Binary Sensor node instead of assuming a default of `OFF`.

Insteon battery devices use a 24hr heartbeat entity to watch if the device is alive or dead. The original logic assumes the device is healthy until a heartbeat is not received within 25 hours. This change fixes the issue where if HA is restarted or the integration is reloaded, the entity which may have had a low battery will show as normal again for up to 25 hours after a restart.

issue_context.title: ISY994 Insteon battery heartbeat nodes don't restore state
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Insteon battery devices use a 24hr heartbeat entity to watch if the device is alive or dead. The original logic assumes the device is healthy until a heartbeat is not received within 25 hours.

This logic was added before it was possible to restore the state of an entity after a Home Assistant restart or integration reload.

The issue: an entity may have a missed heartbeat and report a low battery but if HA is restarted or the integration is reloaded, the device will revert back to normal for up to 25 hours.

Code link: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/c1075ebb8cb98c30fc72c0cf15988f4173ed2b39/homeassistant/components/isy994/binary_sensor.py#L142

@bdraco: I will fix, capturing here so I don't lose track.
